relevance_note: The paper describes three patients with heterozygous TNFAIP3 missense variants and three relatives carrying them, e.g. "He had a heterozygous c.574G>A (p.Glu192Lys) variant of TNFAIP3."
method_note: Read the whole paper including the converted supplementary file; values transcribed by hand into a Python build script, which also generated the 20 checklist rows per person and checked spans. Table 1 and Table 2 have patients/variants as columns; Table 1 column headers are 'P1', 'P2', 'P3' (under 'Patient no.'), Table 2 column headers are 'p.Glu192Lys', 'p.Ile310Thr', 'p.Gln709Arg'. Supplemental Table S1 (flattened in the Markdown) has columns: normal range 2-6 years, P1, normal range >=20 years, P2, P3; only values the legend flags as outside the normal range (bold/arrow) were recorded, as observed features; within-range values were not recorded as excluded. Labels: the text uses 'Patient 1/2/3' more often than 'P1/P2/P3', so 'Patient n' was used; relatives labelled by rule 2. Scope: 3 patients plus the 3 parents stated to carry the same variant. The other parent of each patient was sequenced (WES of 'patient 3 and her parents'; 'Sanger sequencing was performed for the patients and their parents'), but the paper gives no result or other detail for them, so they got no rows. Relatives' variant rows take the variant string printed for the related patient, because the paper says each relative had 'the same variant'; relatives' zygosity is from the Fig. 1 legend ('families with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants'). Inheritance left 'not reported' for all patients: the paper says a parent carries the same variant but never states that the variant was inherited (rule 8). MEFV variants c.329T>C and c.442G>C are attributed to Patient 2 unambiguously and were recorded; no other-gene variants for other people. cohort_size_as_stated = 3 (the study's patients); Patient 1's variant was found when 55 patients suspected of autoinflammatory disease were analysed at Gifu University Hospital, and Patients 2 and 3 came from collaborators, so no total for a screened cohort is stated. Table 1 'Autoantibody | No' for P1 and P2 was read as an explicit word (not a symbol) and recorded as excluded. Mother of Patient 2 and father of Patient 3 'lacked any symptoms': recorded as one excluded feature row each; checklist items left 'not reported' because the statement does not address specific features or laboratory findings. Father of Patient 1's 'recurrent stomatitis' was not counted as 'oral ulcers' (ulcers not stated). Patient 1's repeated tonsillitis/bronchitis were not counted as 'recurrent infections' (not called infections; no significant pathogens detected during fever episodes). Patient 3's CNS involvement (epilepsy, athetoid cerebral palsy after neonatal cardiopulmonary arrest) recorded as observed although the paper attributes the cerebral palsy to the arrest. Patient 3's single fever at 24 years not counted as recurrent fever; facial erythema counted under skin lesions. Age at SLE diagnosis for Patient 3 not recorded: the text attaches 'At the age of 24 years' to the symptoms, not explicitly to the diagnosis. Possible inconsistencies noted: Patient 2's 'Serum inflammatory reactants were negative during the intermittent episodes of fever' versus 'recurrent fever ... with a high level of serum CRP' (read as inter-episode periods; recorded as detail on the CRP row); Results text says DNT, Treg, Th17 and Tfh 'tended to increase' in the patients, but Supplemental Table S1 flags Tfh as decreased in P1 and P3 and DNT as within range in P1; P1's Th1 value 9.75 lies below the stated 2-6-year range 25.0±9.5 but is not flagged (not recorded); text gives the Ile310Thr European allele frequency as 0.0002 while Table 2 gives 0.00002.
